title: Same as Ever
author: Morgan Housel
blurb: Morgan Housel argues that we waste energy trying to forecast events no one can foresee, when the smarter move is to understand the things about people that stay constant across history. Through short, story-driven chapters, he shows how greed, fear, and the stories we tell ourselves repeat in every era. The biggest risks are the ones nobody sees coming, so preparation beats prediction. Happiness depends less on what we have and more on what we expect. A compelling story often beats the plain truth. Long periods of calm quietly encourage the risky behaviour that ends them. Bad news arrives suddenly, while good news builds slowly and goes unnoticed. The practical takeaway is to build a life and finances with room for error, accept that volatility is the price of reward, and anchor decisions to what history shows never changes.

lessons.b: Instead of predicting specific events, focus on the human behaviours that stay the same across every era.

lessons.t: Risk Is What You Don't See
lessons.b: The biggest risks are the ones nobody anticipates, so prepare for surprises rather than trying to forecast them.
How satisfied we feel depends less on our circumstances and more on how they compare with what we expected.
People are persuaded by compelling stories more than by facts, so the best idea doesn't always win.

lessons.t: Calm Plants the Seeds of Crazy
lessons.b: Long stretches of stability make people comfortable taking bigger risks, which eventually creates the next crisis.
issues: scene 3: The narration says the tower of bets 'falls hard' after a small shock, but the final frame shows a short, mostly intact three-row stack with only the top bricks slightly tilted. It reads as a wobble, not a collapse. It is also not a 'tall tower' as the title claims. (fix: Build a taller stack first, then show a visible shock (for example an amber jolt or arrow hitting the base). End on a clearly collapsed state: bricks scattered and rotated on the ground line, with the stack no longer standing.)
